newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA repudiates criticism of Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: DASA repudiates criticism of Eurofighter.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), German partner in the four-country Eurofighter project, on Monday repudiated reports that the military jet was technically not up to scratch.

DASA said in a statement that the reports were "targeted disinformation by irresponsible circles" and added that the jet had passed all technical tests to the satisfaction of the four countries which plan to buy it.
"All test results involving DASA and air force pilots over 400 flights of the seven prototypes have given top marks to system design and flight characteristics," the statement said.
"Based on the continuing optimisation of the system, reports of poor performance are simply wrong."

DASA, part of auto maker Daimler-Benz AG, was reacting to an unsourced report in Monday's Spiegel weekly which said the Eurofighter suffered severe deficiencies in its flight control system and its radar was unable to distinguish between one and several aircraft.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and Finance Minister Theo Waigel are negotiating on how much money to budget next year to pay towards Germany's planned order of 180 Eurofighters.

Partner countries Britain, Italy and Spain are awaiting a firm order from Bonn to enable serial production to start and both Ruehe and Waigel said at the weekend talks on interim financing for the 23 billion mark order were going well.
However, Juergen Koppelin, defence spokesman for junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), said his party had not yet gone along with any coalition deal to buy the Eurofighter.
In a statement, he also referred to problems with the Eurofighter's radar and said its weapons systems had not been developed properly and would cost more money.
Koppelin also demanded the completion of a deal for DASA to repay early government pre-financing aid granted to its Airbus civilian jet operations to help pay for Eurofighter.
"Without a successful result in these negotiations, the procurement and financing of the Eurofighter is completely out of the question," Koppelin said.
